messages.subject: Order the data per population
parts:
Dear Arthur, Dear all, 

i am using dartR on my dart-seq dataset. I managed the filtration and to obtain good representation in analysis as DAPC (with compoplot), I need to roder my individuals per population.
Indeed, my individuals are in disorder (ex. [1] Pacific-SW      Atlantic-SE     Atlantic-SE     Atlantic-SE     Pacific-SW      Pacific-SW      Pacific-SW      Pacific-SW      Pacific-SW      Atlantic-SE     Atlantic-SE    
 [12] Atlantic-SE     Atlantic-SE     Atlantic-SE     Atlantic-SE     Pacific-SW      Pacific-SW      Pacific-SW      Pacific-SW      Pacific-SW      Atlantic-SE     Atlantic-SE    
 [23] Atlantic-SE .....)
Do you have a function to manage this critical point in manipulation of data ?

Thank you very much,

Natacha

messages.author: 8559f272679693c3
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Order the data per population
parts:
Hi Natacha,

A slightly clunky way to do it might be to use the seppop function from adegenet, which will make a separate genlight for each population, and then to recombine these genlight into one. Might be worth a try but I’m sure there are more elegant ways too.
Cheers,
Olly

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Order the data per population
parts:
Hi Tracy,

 

Seppop is still currently dangerous as adegenet has a error in this function. (it separates it but not correctly and you may not notice it).

 

So the better option is to use “base” R commands.

 

Once you filtered all your data set you simply can do:

 

 

 

 

reorderedgl <- gl[order(pop(gl)) , ]

 

 

This orders all individuals in pops in alphabetical order. In case you want to have a different order it is a bit more complicated (relevel the pop factor to the order you like) and then use this in the [, ] (square bracket) function.

 

Cheers, Bernd

messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Order the data per population
parts:
Yes it reorders the metadata as well.

 

The [, ] function works for everything before the comma (based on individuals), do not use it to sort out the order of loci. Here you need to “manually” reorder the loci as well. This is one thing that is still on my todo list (basically writing our own genlight class (obviously inherited from the adegenet genlight, but extending it to our dartR genlight).

 

Until then you can use the [,] for sorting, deleting, subsetting individuals, but not loci.

Cheers, Bernd

Got it! With the help of a colleague:

pop(gl) <- factor(pop(gl), levels = c(particular order you want))
gl_reordered <- gl[order(pop(gl)),]
